messages:
Alyssa: Heads-up — saw a host-side perf regression after last night's kernel-batcher rollout. p99 decode for small requests up ~18%. Traces attached.
Mike: Yep, noticed higher tail on the mini requests dashboard. Quick skim shows extra memcpy/allocs in request parsing + streaming chunker.
Alyssa: Repro steps: 100rps, payloads 1-16 tokens. before: p99 ~30ms, after: ~36ms. KV cache hit-rate steady. CPU in syscall mode +6ppt.
Jorge: Any kernel-selection or batching heuristic changes rolled simultaneously? That could change fast-path choices.
Sasha: I ran a flamegraph. Hot stacks concentrated in parse_token_stream() and grpc slice copies. Short excerpt:
```text
parse_token_stream          42%
grpc_slice_copy             18%
writev_coalesce              6%
alloc_small_buffer          12%
``` 
Sasha: also saw elevated mutex hold times on kv-cache shard locks during bursts.
Mike: probable causes: (1) the new kernel selector prefers a memcpy-path that copies frames for small writes, (2) streaming chunker now re-fragments frames more aggressively -> extra copies.
Emma: quick patch idea: avoid copying when grpc slice count == 1 (common for tiny requests). microbench locally: p99 down ~7% for small reqs.
Alyssa: good. also consider lowering the batch-hint threshold for tiny payloads so they stay single-frame.
Jorge: KV note: shard-level contended locks visible. Add per-shard stats and change eviction jitter to reduce synchronized evict bursts.
Mike: I can prep a PR to (a) toggle smallwrite coalescing, (b) add kernel-selector hint for single-slice fast-path, (c) expose kv shard metrics.
Sasha: I'll run a full perf regression after the PR lands. Quick A/B would be useful: baseline vs smallwrite=false.
Emma: starting canary build with the no-copy patch now.
infra-bot: deploy rd-frontend-canary-3 started by Emma — image:redwood/proxy:canary-20260323 — status: rolling
Alyssa: thanks. other experiments: reduce HTTP2 WINDOW_UPDATE granularity (8k -> 16k) to cut frame count; may reduce per-frame overhead.
Mike: good call. also check gRPC flow control interactions — window tuning sometimes increases fragmentation.
Jorge: one more: kernel selection logs show fallback to generic kernel for sequences <32 tokens after the rollout. need to ensure we prefer quantized memcpy kernel for tiny sequences.
Sasha: noted. I'll add tracing around kernel decision and record sequence-length distribution for the canary traffic.
Emma: uploaded quick perf logs: https://internal/redwood/perf/3321009999 — includes flamegraphs + alloc profiles.
Alyssa: action items: Mike PR (smallwrite toggle + kernel hint), Sasha tracing + regression run, Jorge kv-metrics + eviction jitter tweak, Emma canary + perf link. If canary looks good we'll roll to staging.
Mike: I'll tag the PR @sasha @emma and include microbench numbers & flamegraph. ETA end of day.
Sasha: ack. running suite overnight. :thumbsup: 
Alyssa: thanks team. we'll reconvene in triage tomorrow 10:00 if canary requires manual rollback or further tuning.
